english.title: Possess a drug subject of a Temporary Class Order on board a ship
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were knowingly concerned in the carrying or concealing of a drug subject of a temporary class order, namely **(..SPECIFY THE DRUG AND INCLUDE THE QUANTITY..), on a ship, namely **(..SPECIFY THE SHIP..), to which section 19 of the Criminal Justice (International Co-operation) Act 1990 applied, knowing or having reasonable grounds to suspect that that drug was intended to be imported or had been exported in contravention of section 3(1) of the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971 or the law of any state other than the United Kingdom
english.legislation: Contrary to section 19(2)(b) and (4)(b) of the Criminal Justice (International Co-operation) Act 1990.

investigatoraction.description: Criminal lifestyle offence under Schedule 2 to POCA - consider confiscation order
Submit a form Crimsec 38 where drugs are seized

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) No proceedings without consent of DPP or Commissioners of Customs and Excise.
(ii) No proceedings alleged to have been committed outside the landward limits of the territorial sea of the United Kingdom on a ship registered in a Convention state shall be instituted except with authority of Commissioners of Customs and Excise of the powers conferred by Schedule 3 to this Act; and section 3 of the Territorial Jurisdiction Act 1878 shall not apply to those proceedings.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Fourteen years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
